concepts.def: Smallest unit of matter that keeps the properties of an element; ~10⁻¹⁰ m across.
Tiny dense central region of an atom (~10⁻¹⁵ m) containing protons and neutrons.
Positively charged particle in the nucleus; relative mass 1, relative charge +1.
Uncharged particle in the nucleus; relative mass 1, relative charge 0.
Negatively charged particle orbiting the nucleus in shells; relative mass ~1/2000.
Rutherford's gold-foil scattering replaced the plum pudding model with a small, dense, positive nucleus.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Atomic & Nuclear Physics — a core area of GCSE Physics.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Atomic & Nuclear Physics brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Atomic & Nuclear Physics.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.
